name: Covenant — Verified Reputation & Trust Exchange
description: Covenant is a privately operated reputation verification network founded in 2204 by the data brokerage firm Strata Analytics, designed as an alternative to the Meridian Score's government-adjacent infrastructure. Where the Meridian Score is opaque and bureaucratic, Covenant offers users a transparent, portable reputation ledger — employment history, financial behavior, community vouching, and civic participation — that users theoretically own and control. In practice, Covenant's 'user ownership' model contains deeply buried licensing terms that allow Strata Analytics to sell reputation data in aggregate to Corponation HR systems, housing authorities, and credit institutions, making it a sophisticated data extraction operation dressed as user empowerment.
cultural_impact: Covenant has created a parallel reputation economy in Tiers 2-3 where community vouching and peer verification can, in theory, substitute for formal institutional trust — allowing someone with a damaged Meridian Score to rebuild credibility from the ground up. The platform's darker effect is an intensification of social surveillance, as users are incentivized to vouch for allies and withhold vouches from rivals, turning everyday social relationships into calculated reputation transactions.
key_figures: Daeun Mbeki-Holst (Covenant's public-facing founder, Tier 4 figurehead)
Arlo Szymanski-Oduya (whistleblower, leaked Covenant's data-sale architecture in 2221)
locations: Strata Analytics tower, Tier 4 commercial district
Covenant community verification hubs in Tier 2-3 residential blocks
The Mbeki-Holst Foundation offices, Mid-Meridian civic center
story_hooks: A Tier 2 worker discovers their Covenant vouching history has been algorithmically manipulated — vouches they never gave are attributed to them, tanking the reputation of a labor organizer they've never met — and someone wants to keep them quiet about it.

Arlo Szymanski-Oduya, the whistleblower who leaked Covenant's data-sale model, is found to have a Covenant profile full of damaging fabricated entries — a targeted reputation assassination — and needs someone to help prove the data was planted.

A Tier 3 community is organizing a collective Covenant vouching network to support members facing housing discrimination — but Strata Analytics is legally threatening to classify collective vouching as 'coordinated reputation manipulation' under their terms of service.
user_base: 31 million registered users; primarily Tier 2-3 working adults seeking employment, housing, or credit access; growing Tier 1 adoption among those trying to escape the Gray Zone
monetization: Freemium subscription model for enhanced reputation display features; primary revenue from bulk reputation-data licensing to Corponation HR, housing, and credit systems
notable_feature: Community Vouching Protocol — a peer-verification system that allows users to stake their own reputation score on behalf of another, creating cascading trust networks that can elevate or devastate scores faster than any institutional process
